nodes.title: Wallet login: two simultaneous first logins for one address issue a token for an id that is not in the database (4 of 5 rounds)
nodes.description:
## BLUF

Pre-existing on develop, found by the Opus gate on #1476 (KS-806) and filed at the priority Wednesday asked for. Two concurrent FIRST wallet logins for the same address both succeed with 200, only one row is created, and in 4 of 5 measured rounds one of the two responses carries an access token for a user id that does **not exist** in `users`. `userRepo.createUser` returns the object it was given, not the row `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` actually stored, and `getOrCreateWalletUser` trusts it.

## Recommendation

Make the wallet create path read back the stored row (or `RETURNING` it) and use THAT id, or fail and retry the lookup when the returned row's `wallet_address` does not match. Add a concurrency cell against a real Postgres (Seat J's native recipe). This is the same "fabricated object, not in the table" class KS-806 names; #1476 removes the collision between different wallets but not this race between two requests of the same wallet.

## Detail

* **Measured** (gate probe P4, real Postgres 15 built from the repo's init SQL + 49 migrations, app role `secuura_app` under RLS, the real route, real `/register`, real `userRepo`, real 039 lookup): 5 rounds of `Promise.all([login(A), login(A)])` for a fresh address A. Every round: both statuses 200, exactly 1 row. `idsInDb` per round: `[true,true]` (same id) once, then `[false,true]`, `[true,false]`, `[true,false]`, ... so in 4 of 5 rounds one returned id is not in the table. The token for that id then works until something looks the user up.
* **Where:** `services/auth/src/routes/wallet.ts` `getOrCreateWalletUser` (lookup, then `userRepo.createUser(user)` with a fresh `uuidv4()`), and `userRepo.createUser`'s upsert on `email_lookup_hash` returning its input.
* **Not caused by #1476:** the same shape exists on develop; with the old 8-character email the collision made it worse (every second wallet), with the new email it only happens for a true double submit of one address.
* Evidence: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476/logs/probe_head.out` (line 4) and `gateprobe1476.test.ts` (cell P4).

Provenance: Opus QA gate on #1476, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476/verdict.md` (sha256/16 `b4615b4a35be26fb`), Minor-4; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-806, KS-1460 (`updateUser` callers that discard the result), KS-1052.
